Seattle and Eastside bathrooms

Bathroom remodeling for Seattle and Eastside homes, grounded in waterproofing and craft

Bathrooms concentrate plumbing, ventilation, electrical work, tile, cabinetry, glass, and moisture control in a compact footprint. RT Signature Homes plans those systems together so the room performs as well as it looks.

Request a consultation Explore design ideas
Call (206) 407-6291
Completed RT project photography · Redmond

From Redmond we take qualifying bathroom projects across Seattle and the Eastside, including Bellevue, Kirkland, Redmond, Sammamish, and Issaquah. The office stays in Redmond. Other cities are where the work happens, not extra addresses.

Project fit

The service covers complete primary and guest bathroom renovations, layout changes, accessibility improvements, and replacement of outdated or failing assemblies.

Typical scope

  • Layout, fixture, and storage planning
  • Shower, tub, waterproofing, and drainage systems
  • Tile, vanity, countertop, glass, lighting, and ventilation
  • Accessibility and aging-in-place considerations
  • Plumbing, electrical, inspection, and finish coordination
  • Protection and sequencing while the rest of the house stays in use

Design ideas

Bathroom remodeling inspiration

Explore visual directions alongside the planning, material, and performance decisions that help turn an idea into a buildable project.

Bathroom design ideas

A refined bathroom depends on careful relationships between waterproofing, drainage, tile, fixtures, ventilation, lighting, storage, and clearances. These ideas keep performance and comfort at the center.

Explore the gallery

Treat waterproofing as a system, not a finish.

Substrates, membranes, penetrations, slopes, drains, corners, and transitions are planned before tile patterns are finalized.

The best-looking shower still depends on the work that disappears beneath it. Seattle and Eastside houses add moisture, shaded exposures, and older assemblies that deserve early investigation. We would rather walk the existing bathroom before anyone promises a spa on a napkin.

Improve access without making the room feel institutional.

Curbless entries, practical clearances, seating, blocking, hand-shower placement, and useful lighting can be integrated into a refined design.

The right choices depend on the household and the existing structure. Many Eastside projects also have to keep a hall bath available while the primary bath is apart. Dust control, access, and utility interruptions are part of the plan, not an afterthought.

Seattle, Redmond, and Bellevue use different plan-review and inspection processes. Permits and fee schedules belong to the city that has jurisdiction. Redmond's published building-permit tables are a useful example of valuation-based fees. They are not a bid for your house, and they are not the schedule for every Eastside city. See What remodel permits can cost in Redmond, then confirm the city that actually issues your permit.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Layout changes, tile coverage, glass, and fixture specifications
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements for the applicable city
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, occupancy, and project sequencing

Questions homeowners ask

Bathroom remodeling FAQs

What most affects bathroom-remodel cost?

Layout changes, waterproofing scope, tile coverage, fixture specifications, glass, cabinetry, existing conditions, and the number of trades involved.

Can a tub become a walk-in shower?

Frequently, but drain location, floor structure, waterproofing, ventilation, window placement, and desired shower dimensions must be evaluated.

How do you reduce disruption?

The plan identifies protection, access, material staging, utility interruptions, inspection points, and whether another bathroom remains available.

Do you have a bathroom showroom on the Eastside?

No. Selections happen against your house and the product lines that fit the plan. Design galleries are inspiration, not RT bathrooms.

Can you remodel a hall bath only?

Yes, when it is a fit. We still look at ventilation, waterproofing, and how the bath meets the rest of the home.
